verses.text: Six days later Jesus took Peter, James and James's brother John with him. He led them up a high mountain, where they were alone.
There his appearance was changed in front of them. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became as white as light.
Then Moses and Elijah appeared in front of them, talking with Jesus.
Peter said to Jesus, "Lord, it is good for us to be here. If you want, I will put up three shelters here, one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah."
While Peter was still speaking, a bright cloud covered them. A voice from the cloud said, "This is my Son, whom I love. I am very pleased with him. Listen to him!"
When the followers heard this, they fell face down on the ground, terrified.
But Jesus came and touched them. "Get up," he said. "Do not be afraid."
When they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus.
As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus ordered them, "Do not tell anyone what you have seen until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead."
The followers asked him, "Then why do the teachers of the law say that Elijah must come first?"
Jesus replied, "It is true that Elijah comes first and will put everything right again.
But I tell you, Elijah has already come, and people did not recognise him. Instead, they did whatever they wanted to him. In the same way the Son of Man is going to suffer at their hands."
Then the followers understood that he was talking to them about John the Baptist.
When they came back to the crowd, a man came up to Jesus and knelt in front of him.
"Lord, have mercy on my son," he said. "He has seizures and suffers terribly. He often falls into the fire or into the water.
I brought him to your followers, but they could not heal him."
Jesus replied, "You people have no faith, and you have turned away from God! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring the boy here to me."
Jesus ordered the demon to leave, and it came out of the boy. He was healed from that moment.
Then the followers came to Jesus in private and asked, "Why could we not drive it out?"

He replied, "Because you have so little faith. I tell you for certain, if you have faith as small as a mustard seed, you can say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.
But this kind of demon does not go out except by prayer and fasting."
While they were together in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is going to be handed over to people.
They will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised to life." And the followers were filled with great sadness.
When Jesus and his followers arrived in Capernaum, the men who collected the temple tax came to Peter. They asked, "Does your teacher not pay the temple tax?"

"Yes, he does," Peter replied. When Peter came into the house, Jesus spoke first. "What do you think, Simon?" he asked. "Who do the kings of the earth collect taxes and duties from? From their own children or from others?"
"From others," Peter answered. "Then the children do not have to pay," Jesus said to him.

"But we do not want to offend them. So go to the lake and throw out your fishing line. Take the first fish you catch. When you open its mouth, you will find a coin. Take it and give it to them to pay the tax for you and me."
